statement: If a number have any part whatever, it will be measured by a number called by the same name as the part.
heath_proof: For let the number A have any part whatever, B, and let C be a number called by the same name as the part B; I say that C measures A. For, since B is a part of A called by the same name as C, and the unit D is also a part of C called by the same name as it, therefore, whatever part the unit D is of the number C, the same part is B of A also; therefore the unit D measures the number C the same number of times that B measures A. Therefore, alternately, the unit D measures the number B the same number of times that C measures A. [VII. 15] Therefore C measures A.

**Statement:** If a number have any part whatever, it will be measured by a number called by the same name as the part.

**Step 1.** Let A be a number which has a part, and let the part be called by the same name as a number B. So A has a B-th part. We must show that B measures A.

**Step 2.** Since A has a B-th part, let C be the B-th part of A. By the meaning of a B-th part (D7.3), C measures A, and specifically the unit measures B the same number of times that C measures A. That is, C taken B times equals A.

**Step 3.** Since the unit measures B a number of times equal to B, and C measures A the same number of times (namely B times), by Proposition 7.15, alternately, the unit measures C the same number of times that B measures A.

**Step 4.** Therefore B measures A, which is what was to be proved.
